A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CALM research, with matching authors, architecture, and retained continuation experiments. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech and music compression and continuation experiments, human evaluations, component ablations, and supplementary context-window and scaling studies.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results and adds original text-to-speech, conditioned music generation, TTS ablation, and Pocket TTS evaluations, alongside explicitly attributed baseline results.

M1.justification: v3 adds text/CLAP conditioning, latent classifier-free guidance, and backbone latent distillation (Sections 4.6–4.7), and adopts Lagrangian Self-Distillation for TTS sampling. Pocket TTS distills a 24-layer teacher backbone into six layers while retaining its sampling head. These substantially extend the procedure. The original continuation architecture remains; explicitly adding WavLM distillation to Equation 2 documents a component already described in v1.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates speech and music continuation. v3 additionally evaluates text-to-speech on LibriSpeech test-clean and conditioned music generation using CLAP, including text-to-music evaluation on MusicCaps. These introduce different conditioning requirements and benchmark coverage. The original French/English speech continuation and LAION-Disco music coverage are retained.

E2.justification: New TTS comparisons include F5-TTS, DSM, DiTAR, and SALAD; Pocket TTS additionally includes Chatterbox Turbo and Kokoro. MusicCaps comparisons add MusicLM, AudioLDM2, Noise2Music, Jen-1, MusicFlow, and the original text-conditioned MusicGen. DiTAR/SALAD and several MusicCaps baseline scores are explicitly borrowed from publications. Comparator membership in the original continuation experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces TTS training/evaluation settings, WER/CER and speaker-similarity measurements, MUSHRA evaluations, and PANN-based KLD/CLAP music metrics. Speech compression gains PESQ, STOI, and human evaluation. Pocket TTS uses enhanced 24 kHz inputs for all its baselines, separating that comparison from Table 3. The runtime table also reverses the RTF convention while retaining the measured generation times.

E4.justification: Appendix E.5 adds substantive TTS ablations comparing LSD with consistency and varying absent, text-only, and text-plus-audio guidance. Table 3 adds a reference-through-VAE diagnostic investigating low speaker-similarity scores. The original component, context-window, scaling, sampling-step, temperature, and head-batch analyses are retained; their relocation does not constitute new evidence.

E5.justification: v3 removes the PPX and VERT confidence intervals from Table 2 while retaining their point estimates. It also removes v1's general statement that all reported intervals use 95% confidence. The Bayesian Elo estimation procedure and its 95% posterior intervals remain unchanged. Neither version establishes additional repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for compression, conditioned generation, TTS ablations, and Pocket TTS: examples include CALM's 1.81 WER in Table 3, 2.14 MusicCaps FAD in Table 11, and Pocket TTS's 1.84 WER, tied with DSM, in Table 12. These are newly reported experiments, not gains over v1 under identical settings. Original continuation point estimates and plots remain; changed RTF values reflect the inverted convention.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds the two-time LSD flow-map definition and combined flow-matching/self-distillation objectives. Section 4.6 formalizes latent guidance. Section 4.5 replaces v1's Jacobian-based temperature argument and stated variance 1/sqrt(tau) with standard-deviation scaling by sqrt(tau), correcting the mathematical description without establishing that experiments were rerun. Existing consistency and Bayesian Elo formulations are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the contribution list to include latent guidance and distillation and explicitly claims application to four tasks. The abstract and introduction add the open-source, approximately 100M-parameter Pocket TTS contribution and faster-than-real-time laptop CPU operation. The earlier claim of being the first application across both speech and music is removed; the general efficiency/fidelity thesis remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds a localized explanation attributing poor automatic TTS speaker similarity partly to the VAE and uses human evaluation to qualify that metric. It also discusses guidance-related quality/similarity tradeoffs and LSD's suitability at the tested smaller scale. The original explanations concerning error accumulation, noisy long-term context, clean local detail, and incomplete scaling evaluation remain substantially intact.

D1.justification: v3 documents the 88k-hour TTS dataset mixture, SentencePiece vocabulary, LSD loss-batch allocation, guidance settings, and TTS architecture/training hyperparameters in Table 14. It provides Pocket TTS distillation details and tested CPU models, reports a model release with repository and enhanced evaluation-data links, and promises CALM training code. Existing continuation and VAE hyperparameters are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially broadens positioning through continuous word-sized and spectral speech representations, IMPACT, MingUni-Audio, and other newer work. It connects temperature sampling to GAN truncation, credits latent guidance to SoundReactor, and incorporates Boffi et al.'s LSD framework. It also drops v1's first-across-both-domains assertion and its near-exclusivity statement about accelerating continuous autoregressive sampling.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized around four task evaluations. Music VAE details, the temperature study, and several efficiency analyses move from the main text into dedicated appendices. Noise-injection exposition moves within the method section, temperature sampling is rewritten, and the appendix structure is expanded and reorganized. Much original prose and the conclusion remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds TTS, conditioned-music, MusicCaps, Pocket TTS, and TTS-ablation tables, expands speech-compression metric columns, and adds a TTS hyperparameter column. Several existing tables are relocated or reformatted. All three original figures are retained; the two analysis plots move to the appendix and exchange numbering. Title, headings, running headers, and page layout also change.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens practical validation beyond v1's continuation experiments: conditioned-generation benchmarks and TTS ablations test the new mechanisms, while the distilled Pocket TTS model provides small-model CPU evidence relevant to the original edge-device motivation. Expanded technical documentation and the corrected temperature explanation also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting regressions: PPX/VERT intervals disappear, and Appendix F overstates Table 12, which also marks Kokoro as real-time on CPU and contains no ground-truth row supporting its ground-truth comparisons.
